title: Authenticated RPC/HTTPS publication boundary
summary: Speech dev13 exposes unary control-plane operations through existing RPC Core. The existing HTTPS JSON-RPC gateway owns TLS/HTTP publication and delegates actual identity proof and authorization to the platform LDAP identity authority.
invariants: Speech does not implement HTTP, TLS, JSON-RPC, LDAP or a competing transport selector.
RPC Core registration is explicit and frozen. Public HTTPS JSON-RPC names map only to already-registered Speech RPC Core operations.
The HTTPS gateway authenticates the accepted TLS exchange and authorizes each service operation using platform identity. Speech never trusts caller-supplied headers, roles or JSON principal fields.
Ordinary JSON-RPC is control plane only. Streaming PCM, callbacks and stateful media flow are not published as unary HTTPS JSON-RPC operations.
Remote TTS must not return a server-local temporary path. Output needs an existing durable external reference or an injected material publisher.
Remote STT resolves an externally meaningful material reference through an injected material authority. Without material authority, material operations fail closed.
Connect Selector remains route-selection authority; HTTPS JSON-RPC publication is one optional binding, not a mandatory Speech dependency.
dependencies: optional RPC HTTPS JSON-RPC gateway v0.1-dev1
platform LDAP Identity Directory authority at deployment
